items.title: Why Nvidia couldn't afford to lose Jensen Huang | About That
items.summary_auto: Nvidia's board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, stating the decision followed consultation with multiple stakeholders — including the U.S. government. Andrew Chang breaks down how the CEO of a trillion-dollar tech company returned just 11 days after being forced to step down following reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)

items.title: Pentagon takes fresh aim at Canada's military readiness, defence spending priorities
items.summary_auto: The Pentagon has escalated its criticism of Canada, accusing Ottawa of failing to meet NATO and NORAD obligations and putting domestic economic interests ahead of military effectiveness. The extraordinary public rebuke comes amid mounting tensions over bilateral defence co-operation, military readiness and the Carney government’s review of the F-35 purchase.

items.title: 'I'm not a hero,' says Arizona man who found lost toddler alone in the desert
items.summary_auto: Search parties with helicopters, K-9 units and heat-seeking drones scoured the rural dessert community of Eloy, Ariz. for hours looking two-year-old Vella Campillo after she wandered away from her backyard — all to no avail. Then Jay Stewart found her hiding in a bush.

items.title: Rights group details 'surge' in violent attacks on Palestinian health-care workers
items.summary_auto: Based on testimony from health-care workers, Physicians for Human Rights Israel says there’s been a 350 per cent increase in violence against Palestinian health workers by settlers and the Israeli military. Israel denies the report's claims.

items.title: Canada adds Masar Badil group to terrorist entity list, citing status as alias for Samidoun
items.summary_auto: Canada's public safety minister announced Monday that Masar Badil had been added to the country's terrorist entity list, as an alias for Samidoun, a group which was added to the same list in 2024.

items.title: More transparency needed on surveillance pricing, privacy commissioner says
items.summary_auto: Canada's privacy commissioner says people should be warned when they are being targeted by surveillance pricing.

items.title: Court holds N.L. man over fear he will commit terrorist acts after threats against mosque
items.summary_auto: Facing eight charges and a court application used when there is a “fear of terrorism offence,” Matthew Collins was allegedly making threats against a mosque.

items.title: Legislation would enable Alberta to create a Crown corporation for natural gas transmission
items.summary_auto: The Natural Gas Infrastructure Act, if passed, would also allow the government to create a separate provincial entity to plan natural gas infrastructure in the province.

items.title: How Ukraine destroyed one of Russia's newest warships
items.summary_auto: Ukraine says its naval drones sank one of Russia's newest vessels – the corvette Merkury – in a Libyan port. Seven drones were used in the attack, which also hit a cargo ship which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia used to transport weapons. CBC's Briar Stewart explains what we know about the operation.

items.title: Girl, 14, planned random killing of child at her former Winnipeg elementary school: Crown
items.summary_auto: A teen girl accused of planning to kill a child at her former Winnipeg elementary school was radicalized online and had a romantic fantasy about an American school shooter, a court heard before the teen was granted bail last week.

items.title: Ontario, Alberta premiers weigh in on interprovincial trade, say it remains complicated
items.summary_auto: During a fireside chat held by the Toronto Region Board of Trade, the leaders of Ontario and Alberta said internal trade barriers remain across the country despite moves to open up interprovincial free trade.

items.title: Defence Department tops up cadet program after outrage over cancelled activities
items.summary_auto: The Defence Department will top up the budget of the cadet and junior ranger programs to allow weekend training and other activities to continue into the new year, Defence Minister David McGuinty said on Monday.

items.title: Jennifer Lopez says being Latina limited her early acting roles. Not everyone agrees
items.summary_auto: Jennifer Lopez said being Latina limited her early acting opportunities, prompting her to create roles for herself — a claim that drew online criticism because of her high profile and extensive career.

items.title: Windsor, Ont., hospital ex-employee facing 3 more sex assault charges after patients come forward: police
items.summary_auto: Windsor, Ont., police say new sexual assault charges have been brought against 29-year-old Cody Tyler Desbien, a former hospital ultrasound technician, bringing the count to four after more patients came forward.

items.title: Iranian singer subjected to 74 lashes for performing without her hijab
items.summary_auto: An Iranian singer and four members of her production team have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for "offending public decency ‌by producing and publishing obscene and immoral content online," an Iranian news website said on Monday.

items.title: London, Ont., police solve 1968 murder of teenager Jackie Dunleavy using genetic genealogy
Quebec rallies behind Montreal’s bid for global defence bank headquarters
items.summary_auto: Montreal is competing to host the headquarters of the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), and Quebec's sovereignist government has thrown its full support behind the bid.

items.title: What happened at the Seattle airport? Outrage as ICE arrests man and daughter boarding flight
items.summary_auto: A chaotic scene unfolded at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport Saturday as a father and daughter were detained by masked immigration officers while boarding their flight bound for L.A.

items.title: Brianne Jenner named Hamilton Havoc's first-ever captain
items.summary_auto: Forward Brianne Jenner has been named the first captain in Hamilton Havoc history, the PWHL team said Monday.

items.title: You Can See Everything crosses $100M US worldwide at the box office
items.summary_auto: As Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything makes its way into cinemas around the globe, the buzzy documentary is proving a big-screen draw with international audiences, too, taking in more than $100 million US at box offices worldwide.

items.title: Arriving at Son of a Critch finale 'surreal', says Benjamin Evan Ainsworth
items.summary_auto: He's played a young Mark Critch for the last five seasons on CBC's Son of a Critch. And on Tuesday, Benjamin Evan Ainsworth will tune into the show's finale. Ahead of the finale episode, Ainsworth shared his thoughts and memories of working on the show in Newfoundland and Labrador with the CBC's Jen White.

items.title: Dentist pleads guilty to professional misconduct in 23-year-old's death
items.summary_auto: A Manitoba dentist was found guilty of professional misconduct Monday in connection with a woman's 2024 death, admitting he gave Virginia Blatz much more local anesthetic than the recommended dose.

items.title: 'The land is ours': First Nation intends to mine sand in Manitoba through Sio Silica partnership
items.summary_auto: A Manitoba First Nation is planning to push ahead with a proposed sand mining operation to support a solar panel manufacturing facility, whether the provincial government likes it or not.

items.title: Man charged in Edmonton-area corn maze killing found not criminally responsible
items.summary_auto: A man charged with second-degree murder for a fatal stabbing at an Edmonton-area corn maze has been found not criminally responsible because of a mental disorder.

items.title: U.S. army can detonate Iowa's degraded bomb-making material, federal appeals court says
items.summary_auto: A federal appeals court has cleared the way for the U.S. army to detonate several tonnes of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant, finding that the plan should limit the dispersal of lead dust into the atmosphere and address concerns raised by environmental groups.

items.title: 3 Calgary police officers charged with manslaughter in death of unarmed Blood Tribe man
items.summary_auto: Three Calgary police officers have been charged with manslaughter two years after an unarmed Blood Tribe man died while in police custody.

items.title: FIFA picks American-led bid as 2031 Women's World Cup host
items.summary_auto: FIFA on Monday confirmed the United States will lead a four-nation, regional co-hosting of the 2031 Women's World Cup, and a UK project led by England was ratified for the 2035 edition.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.summary_auto: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO on Monday in a surprise move shortly after rejecting his offer to return. It's the latest twist in the fallout from Huang's admission of an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

items.title: North American stocks soar, recovering half of last week's plunge after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia's CEO
items.summary_auto: Nvidia led a tremendous rally on Wall Street on Monday following the surprise return of Jensen Huang as its CEO. Nvidia's stock finished just shy of its best day since 2000.

items.title: Bell confirms data breach of Virgin Plus, Lucky Mobile. What should customers do?
items.summary_auto: A spokesperson for Bell says customers across its network of subsidiaries, including Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile, were affected by a Nov. 17 breach but no "highly sensitive" information such as credit card numbers or banking information was impacted.

items.title: Tighter funding leaves northern cadets out in the cold
items.summary_auto: The federal government is investing heavily in the North, but some people involved with the cadet program say Department of National Defence is shortchanging northern kids.

items.title: 2 Americans sentenced to life in prison for murder of Quebec couple in Dominica
items.summary_auto: The two Americans convicted of murdering Quebec entrepreneur Daniel Langlois and his partner Dominique Marchand in Dominica in December 2023 were sentenced on Monday to life in prison without parole.

items.title: How will Mark Carney's appeal influence the Yorkton-Melville byelection?
items.summary_auto: The Liberals are running Aaron Kienle, the sitting Mayor of Yorkton, as their candidate in the byelection set for Dec. 7.

items.title: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine was behind attack on Russian warship off Libya
items.summary_auto: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a naval base in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

items.title: A gold mine has created a 'little town' in central Newfoundland — and it's about to get bigger
items.summary_auto: Step inside the Valentine gold mine near Buchans, which is now Atlantic Canada's largest.

items.title: Quebec's legislative session in limbo as court mandates oath to the King
items.summary_auto: A Quebec Superior Court judge has suspended the province’s law that made the oath to King Charles optional, ordering that members of the province's legislature must swear allegiance before sitting at the National Assembly. Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon said Monday he would refuse to take the oath, and that he would fight the ruling.

items.title: Inside India's bold plan to transform its largest slum, Dharavi, into a multibillion-dollar development
items.summary_auto: India's largest slum is being cleared to make room for a modern urban development to include rehabilitated slum housing plus luxury condos and office towers. It's a massive regeneration project, funded by private and public money. But will it work?

items.title: More Canadians are using cannabis daily than are drinking alcohol daily: study
items.summary_auto: Daily use of cannabis has outstripped daily use of alcohol in Canada, with young Canadians at the front of the trend, new data shows. Experts say this generational shift brings some positives, but that many Canadians remain unaware that there are risks with overuse of cannabis.
